transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing, or taking up time from someone who needs it more. I usually just push through things, you know? 

But... well, I guess what finally scared me into making this appointment is that I’ve been having these... these thoughts lately. Nothing dramatic, I promise! Just... sometimes I catch myself thinking, 'If I just didn’t wake up tomorrow, that might be easier.' 

I would never actually hurt myself—I really want to make sure you know that. I'm not a danger or anything, I just... it unsettled me a bit to even think that way. Am I explaining that okay? I just thought I should probably come in and talk to someone about it, just to be safe.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up tomorrow?

Oh, gosh... I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I hope that's an okay answer. I haven't really been keeping track of it or anything. 

I usually just try to brush those thoughts off and focus on work, you know? It's definitely not an every day thing, just... occasionally. So I couldn't give you an exact timeline of when they started. Am I being helpful at all? I'm sorry I don't have a more specific answer for you.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Well... I really hate to complain, and I know everyone gets the blues sometimes. I wouldn't say I'm crying all day or anything like that. But... yes, I suppose I have been feeling a bit down. 

It's just... most mornings lately, I wake up with this heavy, sort of gray feeling. It's almost like all the color has just drained out of the day before I even get dressed to head to the store. 

I always make sure to put on a good face for my team and the customers, of course! I really try not to let it show or affect my work. But... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do lately?

Oh, well... I really try to keep up with my hobbies, I promise. I know it's important to stay active and engaged outside of work. 

I still set out my paints on the weekends, or I'll make plans to go down to my pottery class. I really do try to push myself to do them. But... I don't know, lately, when I actually get there, or sit down at the easel, I just kind of stare at the materials. I just don't feel any of that... that spark I used to feel. 

It's probably just a phase, right? I usually just end up putting everything away so I don't waste the clay or the paint, and go find something productive to do instead. I hope I'm not sounding ungrateful for having the free time to do those things. Is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
How many weeks have you been feeling this way, with the gray feeling in the mornings and not enjoying your hobbies?

Oh, gosh... weeks? Well, I suppose if I really count back... it's probably been a bit longer than a few weeks. I hope you don't think I've just been letting myself go, but... I think this low, flat part has been going on for about six months now. 

It's been long enough that my usual routines, like the art classes, or even my morning walks before my shift... they just stopped feeling restorative. I really kept trying to walk every morning, I promise! But it just hasn't been helping perk me up the way it used to. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right timeline, I really don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you noticed a decrease in pleasure from activities that you normally find enjoyable?

Oh, yes... I think that's what I was trying to explain a moment ago about my art. I'm so sorry if I didn't make it clear before, I know I can ramble a bit! 

But yes, it's exactly that. I still make a point to set out my paints, or I'll think about going down to the pottery studio, because I know I really *should* enjoy it. But when I actually get there... I just sit and stare at the materials. I just don't feel any of that spark I used to get from it. 

I really do want to enjoy things, I promise I'm trying my best to keep at it. Did I explain it a bit better this time?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Oh, I really wish I could say yes to that. I want to be able to tell you that I'm still having fun doing *something*. But... well, like I was just saying about my paints and the pottery... I think that's pretty much how it is with everything right now. 

I'll get things all set up, or I'll make the plans to go do something I usually love, but then I just end up sitting there staring at it all. I just can't seem to find that spark anywhere lately, no matter how hard I try. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terribly negative, and I promise I'm trying my best to snap out of it. I hope it's okay that I don't have a better answer for you right now... is it normal to feel that way about everything?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or sleep lately?

Oh, well... actually, no, I haven't really noticed any big changes there. I hope that's a good thing! 

I've been trying very hard to keep up with my regular meals, even when I'm feeling a bit flat, because I know I need the energy for my shifts at the store. I always make sure I eat, I promise. So my appetite is pretty much the same. 

And my sleep... well, I still go to bed and get up at my usual times. I get my normal seven or eight hours. I'm definitely not just staying in bed all day, even when I might feel like it. I really force myself to stick to a proper schedule, because I know how important that is. 

Is that... is that a good sign? I hope that's helpful to know. I'm just relieved I can give you a positive answer for once!
Do you have days where you feel somewhat better, or is the gray feeling pretty consistent?

Oh, I really try to have better days, I promise I do. I always try to put on a brave face, especially for my team at work. But, well... if I'm being completely honest—and I hope it's alright to admit this—it's been pretty consistent. 

Most mornings lately, I just wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling. It's almost like all the color has just drained out of everything before I even get dressed for the store. 

But I *do* get dressed, and I go in and do my job, I make absolutely sure of that! I don't want you to think I'm just letting things fall apart or giving up. I push through it the best I can. I just... I really wish I could give you a happier answer right now. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Are there any small things that still bring you a little bit of joy or pleasure?

Oh, I... I know you just asked me something similar, and I really, really want to be able to tell you yes. I want to say there's some little thing that makes me smile. But... well, it's just like I mentioned earlier about my art. 

I'll still get my paints all set out on the table, you know? I'll make the effort. Or I'll look at the schedule for my pottery class and tell myself I'm going to go and have a wonderful time. But then... if I do go, or if I sit down at the canvas, I just end up staring at the materials. 

That spark I used to feel, that little thrill of creating something... it's just not there right now. I'm so sorry, I feel like a broken record saying the same negative thing again. I promise I'm trying to find things to enjoy, I really am. I hope you aren't disappointed in me for not having a better update for you... is it okay that I'm still struggling with this?
Has anything particularly stressful happened to you in the last year?

Well, um... I suppose there has been one thing. I try not to let it get to me, I really do, because I know everyone deals with stress at work. But we got a new district manager recently, and... well, things have been a bit tense. 

I want to make sure I'm doing a good job for them, but it's been difficult. And actually, this whole up-and-down stretch with my mood and my energy... it really started around the time all that trouble with the new manager began. So it's been going on for about two months now. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses or blaming someone else for how I feel. I know I need to handle stress better. Does that... does that seem like the kind of thing that could cause all this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you think your mood would improve if the situation with your new district manager were to resolve itself?

I... I don't know, honestly. I've thought about that a lot, actually. I want to say yes, I really do, because then it would just be a simple fix, wouldn't it? If they were to transfer, or if we just figured out how to work together better, maybe this heavy feeling would just lift. 

But... well, if I'm being perfectly honest—and I hope it's okay to say this—I'm not entirely sure it would go away completely. Even on the days when the manager isn't there, or when things actually go smoothly at the store and there's no conflict at all... I still feel so drained. I still come home and just stare at my paints. 

I feel terrible saying that, like I'm not giving myself a chance to get better. I know I should be more optimistic. Do you think... is it normal to feel like fixing the stress wouldn't fix everything else? I just want to make sure I'm looking at this the right way.
How long have you been feeling this low and disconnected from things you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it, this low, flat feeling... it's been hanging around for about six months now. I know I mentioned the work stress starting two months ago, and that definitely made things harder, but... this feeling of just being disconnected, it's been there longer. 

I really tried to push through it at first. I didn't want to make a fuss or seem lazy, you know? But it's been going on long enough that my usual routines—like my art classes, or even just my morning walks—they just stopped feeling restorative a while ago. 

I feel so silly admitting that I let it go on for half a year without saying anything. I just kept hoping I'd snap out of it on my own, and I didn't want to be a bother to anyone. I hope you don't think poorly of me for waiting so long to get help... is it okay that it's been going on for six months?
Have you had two months or more where you felt this low and disconnected from things you usually enjoy?

Yes, um, definitely. Like I was just saying, it's... it's been about six months of this. I know that's well over the two months you're asking about, and I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just wallowing in it. I've tried so hard to keep my chin up. 

But yes, for about half a year now, that low, flat feeling has just... settled in. It's been long enough that even the things I usually love—like my art classes, or just taking my morning walks—they haven't felt restorative in a long time. I just go through the motions. 

I feel awful even admitting it's been going on that long. I really should have tried harder to pull myself together sooner. I hope I'm answering your question right... does that make sense, that it's been six months?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed any big changes. I try to eat pretty healthy most of the time—lots of salads and things—so my weight has stayed pretty much the same. 

I know sometimes people eat more or less when they're stressed, and I really hope I'm doing okay in that department. I always try to make sure I'm taking care of myself, you know? So, no, my clothes still fit the same. Is... is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had at least two weeks where you felt this low and disconnected from things you usually enjoy at any point in the past six months?

Yes, um, definitely. I know we just talked about this, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much... I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly. 

But yes, like I mentioned, it's been going on for about six months now. So it's definitely been longer than two weeks. I really did try to just push past it, you know? I kept up with my morning walks and my art classes for a while, hoping they would help me bounce back, but eventually, they just stopped feeling restorative. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm giving you the same answer again... but yes, it's been a solid six months of this flat feeling. I hope that's the information you needed?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in, no matter how small?

I really try to find things, I do. I don't want to be someone who just sits around complaining, you know? So, um, I still make the effort. I'll set out my paints at home, or I'll get all ready to go to my pottery class... I always try to keep up with it. 

But lately, when I actually get there, or sit down at my table... I just kind of stare at the materials. I don't feel any of the spark I used to feel. It's just gone. 

I feel terrible even saying that out loud, like I'm just being ungrateful or not trying hard enough to enjoy my life. I promise I really am trying to find the good in things. Is... is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not sounding too negative, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you had at least two weeks in the past six months where you felt this low and disconnected nearly every day?

Um, yes, I think so. I know I've been talking about this a lot, and I really hope I'm not overstating things... I know everyone has bad days, and I don't want to sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself. 

But, um, yes, nearly every day. Most mornings lately, I wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling. It's like all the color has just drained out of everything before I even get dressed to go to the store. I try to put on a good face for the staff, I really do, but that heaviness is just there, day after day. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic. I just want to make sure I'm answering you honestly. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt significantly better, with little to no symptoms of depression, at any point during the past six months?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I wish I could say yes, because I really do try to snap out of it. I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it for six months straight. 

I'll have a day here or there where I can sort of push through and get things done at work, and I'll think, "Okay, maybe I'm finally turning a corner." But it never really lasts for two whole weeks. The heavy feeling always kind of creeps right back in. 

I feel bad saying no, like I'm not making any progress. I really am trying to be positive, I promise. Is it normal that it just kind of lingers like this? I hope I'm not being a difficult case for you.
Have you experienced an episode of depression like this before?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt a little stressed or down, you know, just from work or life things. But never anything quite like this, where it just stays and stays. 

I hope that's an okay answer. I mean, I'm trying to think back, and I really don't want to give you the wrong information. But I've always been pretty good at just keeping my chin up and pushing through. This is the first time I've felt like I just... couldn't. I feel a little silly even being here for it, to be honest. Is it okay that this is the first time it's happened?
